result:
None of the three solutions has the correct final answer, because all three conclude that no such k exists. I did not derive the smallest k in full, but the "none exist" claim fails for a structural reason.

When n goes to n+1, the digit sum either rises by exactly 1 (no carry) or drops (a carry). A digit sum therefore cannot jump upward past a multiple of 2025. Within any long run of consecutive integers, the sum can only get from below 2025 to above it by landing on 2025, or by dropping at a carry.

Each solution's "avoiding block" is only a block of length up to about 10^224. Each of them hand-waves the case of larger k ("more elaborate construction", "more advanced arguments") without giving any construction. The claim that the set of numbers with digit sum divisible by 2025 is "not syndetic" is asserted without proof, and it appears to be false. Solutions 1 and 3 also contradict themselves: their stated final answers ("1" and "2025") disagree with their boxed "none exist".

I recall that this problem has a finite answer (I believe 1980), though I did not verify that value here. Either way, "none exist" is not correct, and the answers 1, 2025 and "k" are not correct either.

CHOICE: NONE
